newsitem.title: LESOTHO: Lesotho army ends police mutiny.
newsitem.headline: Lesotho army ends police mutiny.

text.p: Lesotho army troops on Sunday ended a 11-day-old police mutiny after overwhelming the rebels with an onslaught of heavy gunfire, resulting in at least 30 officers surrendering to troops.
"Now everything is okay. It is over. They (the renegade police officers) have all been taken," an army major on the scene told Reuters.
The major, who refused to give his name, said the rebel police officers were being held at an army base some two km (one miles) outside the southern African mountain kingdom's capital Maseru.
"Nobody was killed and nobody was wounded. We have arrested about 30 people. They were taken to the Lesotho Defence Force camp," he said. He would not give details of the operation.

Heavy gunfire erupted in the southern African kingdom's capital early on Sunday and a Reuters correspondent on the scene said heavy-calibre machineguns, automatic rifles and hand grenades were being used.

The mutiny began when eight officers seized control of the police headquarters in Lesotho, which is surrounded by and reliant on the region's economic giant South Africa. Up to 60 other policemen were reported to have joined them in occupying the police headquarters.
